messages:
maya (oncall): :rotating_light: seeing a surge of OOMs and CUDA errors from continuous-batcher in us-west-2. multiple containers restarted, customers reporting 20s+ tail latencies. paging now. attaching initial logs below.

luke (eng-runtime): on it. can you paste the nvidia/cuda errors and pod names? rough counts?

maya (oncall): about 6 pods restarted in the last 4m on node ip-10-0-2-45 and ip-10-0-2-46. sample from kubelet logs:

```
E0305 12:07:22.123 kubelet] container "batcher-runtime" OOMKilled
2026-03-05 12:07:22 CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION at /runtime/infer/attn_kernel.cu:428
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

maya (oncall): and pod events:

```
kubectl -n runtime get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=batcher-rt-5f8d
Warning  BackOff    2m (x6 over 3m)    kubelet    Back-off restarting failed container
Normal   Killing    1m                 kubelet    Killing container with id containerd://... system OOM
```

tara (eng-sre): :eyes: are these nodes showing GPU ECC or mem errors? can you run `dmesg | tail` and `nvidia-smi -q` on the node(s)?

ben (infra): i'm already SSHing into ip-10-0-2-45. preliminary nvidia-smi shows GPU memory at ~98% shortly before crash, but no ECC errors in `nvidia-smi -q` yet. we'll dump `dmesg` now.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-BATCHER-MEM-SURGE, severity=P2, owners=@maya @luke. Pager alert sent.

pagerbot: Pager duty notification: oncall maya paged. escalation policy: runtime-ops.

luke (eng-runtime): hypothesis: continuous-batcher KV prefetch/cache growth is allocating more GPU memory per request than expected under this workload. backpressure not kicking in, batch window keeps expanding => per-batch allocation skyrockets.

maya (oncall): agree. we saw the batch size metric jump from ~8 to ~120 in ~40s before the first OOM. logs show continuous-batcher accumulator didn't flush.

luke (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations:
- reduce `batcher.max_batch_window_ms` to 10ms for us-west route
- disable KV-prefetch for that model variant
- scale up pool by 2 nodes (add capacity)

can someone run the two quick toggles? i can do the config changes if infra helps with node spin.

ben (infra): scaling + draining plan: i'll bring 2 spare g4dn nodes online in us-west-2 and attach to runtime pool. ETA ~5m. once healthy, we can drain ip-10-0-2-45 to reduce noisy neighbor risk.

tara (eng-sre): suggestion: cordon+drain the highest-restart node after new nodes are up, but don't reboot until we've stabilized 10m to collect coredumps. coredumps might help root cause. also enable `oom_kill_disable`? (we usually avoid tampering) Better: collect gcore on crash and preserve container logs.

luke (eng-runtime): i'll flip batching config from the control plane. new config snippet I'll apply:

```
route: us-west-2
batcher:
  max_batch_window_ms: 10
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  prefetch_enabled: false
```

maya (oncall): applied config change at 12:10 UTC. observed batch size drop to 6-12 within 30s. one node still OOMed during transition.

amelia (customer-success): getting a hit from Customer AcmeCorp. they're seeing 502s in the dashboard and are asking if this is a region thing. rough % of requests impacted?

maya (oncall): rough: ~7% of requests in us-west 12:06-12:14 had errors/timeouts. global requests unaffected. we'll follow up with more precise numbers after rate limiter logs.

luke (eng-runtime): good. we'll keep prefetched KV disabled for the affected model while we triage. next: collect full container logs + `gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt" -p <pid>` on the crashed process if core available.

ben (infra): new nodes are healthy and joined cluster at 12:15. draining ip-10-0-2-45 started.

maya (oncall): while draining, another pod on ip-10-0-2-46 threw a CUDA driver error (below). replaying from kube logs:

```
[2026-03-05 12:13:11] runtime ERROR: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED at /runtime/kernel.cu:212
stack: 0x7fff..., 0x4ab12, 0x7f9c...
```

luke (eng-runtime): is the kernel launch failing because of prior device state (e.g., OOM left device in an inconsistent state)? We should restart the CUDA driver on node after draining.

tara (eng-sre): agree, but driver restarts are impactful. plan: drain node fully, preserve coredumps, then `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` and `modprobe -r nvidia`/`modprobe nvidia`. Ben, can you schedule that after drain completes?

ben (infra): yes. will restart driver on ip-10-0-2-46 at 12:22 post-drain. will keep one node offline for 10m for observation.

amelia (customer-success): telling AcmeCorp we're on it: partial degradation in us-west, mitigation in progress. will update again in 15m.

luke (eng-runtime): follow-up debug: adding a temporary guard in runtime that caps per-batch GPU alloc to 12k tokens and fails new batch additions with 429 if exceeded. will push a hotfix rollout to hosted control-plane for us-west only.

maya (oncall): hotfix applied at 12:18. seeing no new OOMs since batch cap and prefetch disable. tail latency back to <600ms for majority, occasional 3s spikes still observed.

tara (eng-sre): collecting coredump from ip-10-0-2-45 now. uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0312/batcherdump.tar.gz

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0312 updated: mitigation=partial, status=investigating, runbook_step=collect_coredumps

luke (eng-runtime): next steps for root cause: reproduce with loadtest that mimics AcmeCorp traffic (burst + long prompts), instrument allocation paths, run under ASAN/UBSAN build to catch illegal instr or memory issues. also review recent change to continuous-batcher prefetch heuristics rolled 2 days ago.

maya (oncall): customer impact note for pager: AcmeCorp had ~15 failed requests in 8m window. global SLA impact below threshold but still customer-visible. CS team notified.

amelia (customer-success): AcmeCorp responded: appreciate quick action, will await follow-up. asked for a postmortem once done.

ben (infra): driver restart on 10-0-2-46 completed, node rejoined at 12:30. no further CUDA errors observed on that node.

luke (eng-runtime): i'm going to keep prefetch disabled for 24h and leave batch cap in place until we validate a patch. will schedule a canary rollout with an instrumented build tomorrow.

maya (oncall): handing off to night oncall @luke-night for follow-up. summary for handoff:
- incident INC-2026-0312: continuous-batcher batch growth -> OOM/CUDA errors in us-west-2
- mitigations: reduced max_batch_window_ms, disabled KV prefetch, applied batch-size cap, scaled cluster + drained flaky nodes, collected coredumps
- customer impact: partial degradation to AcmeCorp (~7% of us-west requests) — CS loop closed for now
- artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0312/ , coredump tar, kube events, applied config diff
- recommended next actions: loadtest repro, instrument, revert only after canary validated

luke (eng-runtime): got it, i'll pick this up. documenting follow-ups in the incident doc and creating a postmortem channel. leaving the batch cap and prefetch disabled until we've validated patch.

tara (eng-sre): +1 on postmortem. suggest including memory-accounting heatmaps and a timeline of batch-size vs GPU free memory.

amelia (customer-success): I'll schedule a customer-facing summary for AcmeCorp once postmortem draft is ready.

maya (oncall): thanks team. closing paging loop. if anything new, ping the incident channel.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0312: severity downgraded to P3, status=stabilized at 12:40 UTC.

luke (eng-runtime): leaving action items: (1) reproduce under load (2) instrument allocator (3) patch prefetch heuristics (4) run canary. will update incident doc with ETA for patch by EOD tomorrow.

maya (oncall): handoff recorded. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
